LESSON: READING FOR FLUENCY

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: MANDARIN
Strand: Reading 2.1 Reading for Fluency (2 lessons) • Comprehension • Fluency(speed) By 
Topic 2.2: Reading for Fluency
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading for Fluency, part of Reading 2.1 Reading for Fluency (2 lessons) • Comprehension • Fluency(speed) By  in Grade 8 MANDARIN.

Key inquiry question: How does reading fluency enhance communication?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read simple texts and underline words and phrases related to extended family members (e.g. 叔叔 Shūshu , 姑姑 Gūgu, 舅舅 Jiùjiu, 阿姨 Āyí, 堂弟 Tángdì, 表妹 Biǎomèi , 姐夫 jiěfū, 嫂子 Sǎozǐ etc.),

2. read aloud simple paragraphs and underline names of different professions (e.g. 老师;医生;护士 etc.),

3. answer questions from texts about the name, age, profession/occupation of extended family members,

4. read aloud the names of professions collaboratively,

5. take turns to read paragraphs loudly and assess peers’ pronunciation of words collaboratively,

6. compare and contrast naming of extended family members in Chinese, English and Kiswahili and discuss findings with peers.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read simple texts and underline words and phrases related to extended family members (e.g. 叔叔 Shūshu , 姑姑 Gūgu, 舅舅 Jiùjiu, 阿姨 Āyí, 堂弟 Tángdì, 表妹 Biǎomèi , 姐夫 jiěfū, 嫂子 Sǎozǐ etc.),
2. read aloud simple paragraphs and underline names of different professions (e.g. 老师;医生;护士 etc.),
3. answer questions from texts about the name, age, profession/occupation of extended family members,
4. read aloud the names of professions collaboratively,
5. take turns to read paragraphs loudly and assess peers’ pronunciation of words collaboratively,
6. compare and contrast naming of extended family members in Chinese, English and Kiswahili and discuss findings with peers.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading for Fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and Collaboration: teamwork skills are exhibited when the learner reads out names of different professions

collaboratively.

Values:
Unity: the learner takes turns to read aloud paragraphs and assess each other’s pronunciation.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Peer education and mentorship: the learner receives constructive feedback on their fluency when they take turns to read

paragraphs for their peers to assess their pronunciation of words.

• Cultural awareness is enhanced as the learner compares naming of extended family members in Chinese, English and

Kiswahili.

Link to Other Learning Areas:

The learner links their learning to English and Kiswahili on the importance of pronouncing words properly for fluency.
